claims.text: Dynamic mechanical behavior in Co-free, as-solidified FeNiCrMn is governed by a rate- and temperature-dependent transition from dislocation glide to deformation twinning.
High strain rates increase the propensity for deformation twinning in as-solidified FeNiCrMn.
Low temperatures increase the propensity for deformation twinning in as-solidified FeNiCrMn.
Enhanced deformation twinning increases strain hardening.
Enhanced deformation twinning preserves ductility under high-rate or low-temperature loading.
At lower strain rates and higher temperatures, deformation is dominated by dislocation slip.
At higher strain rates or lower temperatures, enhanced twin nucleation becomes the favored deformation mechanism.
Under quasi-static loading at ambient temperature, the alloy deforms primarily by dislocation slip and has a lower twin density.
Above an unspecified threshold strain rate or below an unspecified critical temperature, twin density will increase markedly.
The increase in twin density will coincide with an inflection in the strain-rate sensitivity of yield strength.
The increase in twin density will coincide with an inflection in the strain-rate sensitivity of ductility.
Outside the specified temperature and strain-rate ranges, diffusion-based processes or phase transformations may influence deformation.
